correctness.rationale: Direct Fourier calculation of the |t| coefficients gives a positive-definite Toeplitz matrix; Fejér–Riesz makes the Rayleigh minimum exact. Irreducible Perron–Frobenius ensures a single positive symmetric minimizing spectral factor. A bandwise Fourier identity for sampled step functions, explicit alias tail estimates, strong L2 compactness and smooth recovery samples establish the killed-Cauchy limit. The zero-extended sine function has exactly the stated energy and fails the associated Euler–Lagrange equation logarithmically at the boundary; a smooth perturbation proves strict inequality. The included checker passed 248 finite tests but is not a substitute for these arguments.

value.rationale: The new statement optimizes a natural full class of positivity- and mass-preserving circular approximants, uniquely classifies finite-degree extremizers and provides a nonlocal operator limit with a strict improvement over the explicit Rivlin-type constant. It distinguishes restricted-convolution design from unconstrained best approximation and gives a reproducible spectral route for future kernel design.
